answer: Proof of Personhood protocols utilize cryptographic attestations to anchor identity to a unique kernel of human biological data. This mechanism mandates that agents operate within a sparse, high-cost tundra of verifiable social graphs, effectively raising the capital requirement for identity replication. Any attacker attempting to inflate a plume of fake nodes must incur prohibitive transaction fees and social vetting costs, ensuring the network remains resilient against automated, low-cost Sybil expansion.
